How to draw a page — component rules, buffer.data, styling. Read before view_create.

mime.title: RFC 6838 media type (type/[tree.]subtype[+suffix])
mime.description: What the buffer IS — the kind the client picks a renderer by. Example: "text/markdown"

data.description: The payload a view reads at buffer.data — whatever the source destructures. Example: { title: "Flamingo", summary: "Six species on four continents.", sources: [{ title: "Wikipedia", url: "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamingo" }] }

source.description: Content bytes for a content buffer, written as a File. Example: "# Q3\n\nRevenue …"

turn.description: The turn the buffer surfaces under. Example: "01a0856f-425f-72b8-b36f-decc1bb2050e"

name.description: The short display name the operator reads on the line — a subject, not a sentence. Example: "Flamingo — six species"

description.description: One sentence on what the thing holds, for the tooltip and the list. Example: "Range, diet and the six species, from Wikipedia and two field guides."

label.description: The name and one-line description the operator reads on the buffer's entry in the chat and in the buffer list. Example: { name: "Flamingo", description: "Six species, range and diet" }

items.description: The view's name inside this mode — one view per (slug, mime); the same slug again rewrites it. Example: "pulse"

views.description: Slugs of this mode's views to pin on the buffer. Example: ["pulse"]

effect.valence: Open a buffer on the operator's screen: a working area with a mime, live data, and the files it loads. Pass `data` for a state the mode's views render, or `source` for content (markdown, org, html) the client renders by mime — a source becomes a File this mode holds. `views` pins this mode's views by slug so the buffer shows them instead of the mode's default; `turn` hangs the buffer under that turn. Returns the buffer row — its id is what buffer_update and buffer_label take.

data.description: Data keys to merge over buffer.data; keys you omit stay. Example: { summary: "Six species on four continents." }

source.description:
New content for the file this buffer loads, whole. Example: "# Q3 · final

Revenue …"

effect.valence: Write a buffer — the shared working surface between you and the user. Pass the buffer id and a data patch; the patch merges over the existing data keys. For a content buffer pass `source` instead: the file it loads is rewritten, same row, new hash. This thread's id is in the runtime row of your context; its buffer ids come from entity_find { entity: "buffer", where: { thread } }, or from the thread section when your primer carries one. Returns { message, buffer: [{ id, index, status, mime, data, trait }] }. Example: { id: "01a09010-18e0-736f-ad3f-a65b44d3fa43", data: { summary: "Six species on four continents." } }

name.description: The short display name the operator reads on the line — a subject, not a sentence. Example: "Flamingo — six species"

description.description: One sentence on what the thing holds, for the tooltip and the list. Example: "Range, diet and the six species, from Wikipedia and two field guides."

effect.valence: Name a buffer. The label is what the operator reads on the buffer's line in the chat and in the buffer list — set it when a buffer's subject is clearer than its name, or when the operator asks. Returns { message, buffer: [{ id, index, status, data, view, trait }] }. Example: { id: "01a0856f-425f-72b8-b36f-decc1bb2050e", label: { name: "Flamingo", description: "Six species, range and diet" } }

slug.description: The page's name inside this mode — the subject, kebab-cased; the same slug again rewrites the page. Example: "flamingo"

mime.title: RFC 6838 media type (type/[tree.]subtype[+suffix])
mime.description: What the code is — always application/vnd.viva.dom.svelte+javascript here. Example: "application/vnd.viva.dom.svelte+javascript"

source.description: The complete Svelte 5 component source, exactly as it would sit in a .svelte file. No fences, no prose around it, no partial component. It must open with `<script>\n  let { buffer, terminal } = $props();\n</script>`, hold one root `<article class="page">`, and end with a scoped `<style>` block. See the HOUSE RULES in your context for the frame and the tokens.

effect.valence: Draw a page. Submit a COMPLETE Svelte 5 component as `source`; it is compiled, content-addressed and stored as a View of this mode. Then buffer_create with `views: [slug]` and the page's `data` and `label` puts it on the operator's screen as a line they can click open. The HOUSE RULES in your context are binding — a component that invents its own styling renders wrong, and one that imports from a URL is refused outright. The same slug again rewrites the page in place; view_update does the same.

slug.description: The page's name inside this mode — the subject, kebab-cased; the same slug again rewrites the page. Example: "flamingo"

mime.title: RFC 6838 media type (type/[tree.]subtype[+suffix])
mime.description: What the code is — always application/vnd.viva.dom.svelte+javascript here. Example: "application/vnd.viva.dom.svelte+javascript"

source.description: The complete Svelte 5 component source, exactly as it would sit in a .svelte file. No fences, no prose around it, no partial component. It must open with `<script>\n  let { buffer, terminal } = $props();\n</script>`, hold one root `<article class="page">`, and end with a scoped `<style>` block. See the HOUSE RULES in your context for the frame and the tokens.

effect.valence: Iterate a page you already drew: the SAME view, by slug, gets new source and every buffer showing it re-mounts in place; the buffer's data changes through buffer_update, its line through buffer_label. The HOUSE RULES still bind; a URL import is still refused. Use view_read first if you no longer have the source; revise from it rather than rewriting.

slug.description: The view's name inside this mode — one view per (slug, mime); the same slug again rewrites it. Example: "pulse"

mime.title: RFC 6838 media type (type/[tree.]subtype[+suffix])
mime.description: Which of the slug's rows when it has one per mime; the only one when left out.

effect.valence: Read a view back by slug: the row, its Files, and the source you wrote, so you can view_update it instead of rewriting it from memory.

mime.title: RFC 6838 media type (type/[tree.]subtype[+suffix])
mime.description: Only the rows of this mime when given.

effect.valence: The views this mode holds — each row with its id, slug, mime and entry. Use it to find the slug to view_update or view_read, or to pin with buffer_create.

The live vivalence setup on this machine, as JSON — the same record `viva instance/doctor` prints, read straight off paladin. You already have the standing facts in front of you: the instance, the daemon, the modes and their routes. This is everything under them, in three parts. `daemon` is the one you are running inside: its manifest, the modes it resolved with their traits and routes, the datamap and the entities it opened, the hallucinators it declared and which secret slots each wants, the cortex faculties actually attached, and anything left dormant for want of a key. `ledger` is the machine's own record: where it lives, every instance shelved on it with the one you are inside marked, the services and clients this instance declares, every environment variable by name and whether it resolves, and which declared slots came back unset. `registry` is every module the system resolves, as @owner/type/slug with versions and traits — the standard library plus whatever was tapped. Secrets live in a separate store and never appear here; you get slot names, never a value, and for the environment names only, never what they hold. It is a big record and it stays in this conversation once you pull it, so pull it when a question is about this machine — and then it is the record, not a guess.

query.description: The subject as an article would be titled, plain words, no operators. Example: "flamingo", not "tell me about flamingos".

count.description: How many results to return. Leave it out — eight is enough to orient. Pass a number only when a first pass missed and you want to go deeper.

effect.valence: Search Wikipedia, the English encyclopedia. No key, no account. Every result is an article: its title, its address and a snippet of the matching text. Snippets are fragments, so open any article you intend to quote with web_read — an opened article carries the links in its body, and following them is how you get from a subject to its neighbours. Wikipedia is strong on anything with a name — people, places, species, events, ideas — and thin on the very recent, the very local and anything not yet notable; say so when a query lands outside what it holds. Search matches titles first, so ask for the subject as an article would be titled. Zero results is an answer: say the encyclopedia holds nothing rather than asking again for the same thing. Text is CC BY-SA 4.0 — name the article when you quote it. Example: { query: "flamingo" }.

url.title: RFC 3986 URI with an authority (scheme://…)
url.description: The full address to read, copied from a search result. Only http and https, only public addresses. Example: "https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/security/".

effect.valence: Open one URL and read the article out of it — navigation, sidebars and footers removed, the body returned as markdown with its headings and lists intact. Also returns the links found INSIDE the article, so you can follow a citation without re-searching, and `images` — every in it as { alt, src }, src already absolute https — the ONLY place a src for a figure may come from. `chars` tells you how much text the page held: a few hundred means a stub, not a subject — say so rather than writing a page out of it. `truncated: true` means the page was longer than what you got, and `title` is the document's own title, read off the page and never guessed. A read is expensive and stays in this conversation for every later turn, so open a page you mean to use rather than one you are curious about, and never re-open a page already in this thread — its text is still here. got. Example: { url: "https://docs.deno.com/runtime/" }.

brief.description: The whole brief, in prose. Name what to research, who is asking, what they already know, and any angle the page should take. Example: 'Flamingos, for an operator new to this demo who knows no biology. Cover taxonomy, the six species, and why they are pink and stand on one leg.'

effect.valence: Research a subject and leave a page about it on the operator's screen. It searches Wikipedia, opens the article and follows its links to the neighbours that matter, and draws a report into a buffer the operator can click open in the chat. It returns what it learned, so you can answer from it directly; the page is already on screen by then. Use this when the operator wants to KEEP something. For a single fact, call web_search yourself. It costs a minute and several model calls — one call per subject, not one per question. If it comes back with condition ERROR and a buffer, the page IS on screen and the researcher stopped before summarising: answer from the page, and treat `message` as partial.

entity.description: Entity type from the no-argument listing. Example: "buffer"

effect.valence: Ground yourself before querying. No arguments: every entity on this daemon with row counts and card fields — buffer, thread, turn, literal, symbol and whatever else it opened. With entity: its columns, relations, filter operators, repository extensions and the card projection. Returns { entities: [{ type, rows, card }] } without an argument, { schema: { entity, rows, columns, relations, operators, extensions, card } } with one. Example: { entity: "buffer" }

entity.description: Entity type — list them via entity_schema. Example: "buffer"

where.description: MikroORM filter over the entity's columns and relations; operators $eq $ne $in $nin $like $gt $gte $lt $lte $and $or $not. Example: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337", status: { $in: ["PENDING", "ACTIVE"] } }

fields.description: card: the repository's lean projection (id, slug, traits unless it declares its own); full: every column. Example: "full"

offset.description: Rows to skip — pass next.offset back. Example: 12

effect.valence: Query any entity on this daemon — the buffers on a thread, a thread's turns, literals by slug. Rows come back as cards — the lean agent projection; fields full only when a card lacks something you need. Columns, operators and extensions via entity_schema. Page by passing next.offset back as offset. Returns { <entity>: [rows], total, next?: { offset } }. Example: { entity: "buffer", where: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337" }, fields: "full" }

entity.description: Entity type — list them via entity_schema. Example: "buffer"

where.description: MikroORM filter, the same shape entity_find takes. Example: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337" }

effect.valence: Count matching rows without loading them — cheap grounding before a find. Returns { count }. Example: { entity: "buffer", where: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337" } }

entity.description: Entity type — list them via entity_schema.

where.description: MikroORM filter naming the one entity, the shape entity_find takes.

trait.description: trait data by name, merged deep over what the entity holds

effect.valence: Write trait data on one entity of this daemon — a literal's translation, a buffer's label. Pass the entity type, a where naming the one entity, and a trait patch keyed by trait name; the patch merges deep over the held data, a new name joins its traits. Find the entity first via entity_find. Returns { message, <entity>: [the entity] }.

trait.description: Trait data to merge, keyed by trait name. Example: { LABELED: { name: "Q3 filings", description: "the filings correspondence" } }

effect.valence: Write a thread's trait data — its configuration surface. Pass the thread id and a trait patch keyed by trait name (e.g. MASKED query data); each named trait's data merges over the existing value. This thread's id is in the runtime row of your context. Returns { message, thread: [{ id, phase, traits, trait, counter }] }. Example: { id: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337", trait: { LABELED: { name: "Q3 filings" } } }

Every mode of this daemon with its paths on disk — source, mountpoint, files — as rows: the absolute paths fs_* and shell_run take. The first row is the daemon and its mountpoint. Narrow by type or slug. Returns { message }. Example: { type: "office" }

nature.description: A nature from the primer index. Example: "guides/render"

effect.valence: Reads one deferred section of your primer by its nature, as listed under [primer]. Returns { message }. Example: { nature: "guides/render" }
